gates.sentence: The period of 829.3 days is 4.1 resolution elements from the nearest calendar period (one year); that is clear of it.
The observing pattern has 1% of its power at this period; the sampling does not explain the signal.
Removing any one of 8 years moves the phase by at most 0.04 cycles and the amplitude by a factor of 0.69 to 1.30; the most important year carries 60% of the evidence. The signal depends on one year.
The 2 bands in which the signal is visible agree in phase to within 0.10 cycles.
Searched alone, the first 70% of the time span finds the same period (618.7 days), and its periodic model predicts the remaining 143 points worse than no periodic model (log-likelihood gain -10.1).
With the time axis warped at random, the search does as well as in true time 21.4% of the time; the variation does not clearly keep time.

sentences: The best periodic model has a period of 829.3 days and covers 3.2 cycles in 438 points over 2654 days; its fundamental has an amplitude of 0.37 in the standardised units of the merged light curve (1 is the object's own scatter), and 47% of its power is in higher harmonics.
Against red noise fitted to this object, with the search over 317 trial periods included, the probability of a periodic model this good is 1 in 1,001 (0 of 1000 simulated nulls matched it).
After recalibration against the whole population searched, the probability is 0.01.
For contrast, a test that assumes white noise would have given 1 in 838; that number is not evidence, because the noise is not white.

what_would_change_this: New data are the test. If the period is real, the periodic model fitted now will fit data taken later better than red noise alone; if it is a red-noise bump, it will not. No prediction was recorded for this object, because it was not promoted.
